subject: Re: Encord & Rise Up Labs - POC thread
text:
*Hi Winnie,*

I hope you've been doing well.

I wanted to reach out and reconnect regarding the opportunity to work
together again.

First, I'd like to acknowledge that our last engagement did not meet
the standard
that either of us expected. We take full responsibility for that outcome,
and we've spent time reflecting on what went wrong and, more importantly,
how to improve.

Since then, we've significantly strengthened our approach to AI data
operations. We've built a more experienced annotation team, introduced
tighter screening and QA processes, improved project supervision, and
established a much stronger operational framework to ensure consistent
quality and delivery.

With these improvements in place, I wanted to ask if you'd be open to
giving us another opportunity, starting with a *very small POC*. We believe
this is the best way to demonstrate the progress we've made and rebuild
your confidence in our capabilities without requiring a significant
commitment from your side.

If the POC meets your expectations, we'd be delighted to discuss broader
collaboration. If not, you'll have a clear evaluation with minimal risk.

We truly value the opportunity to work with Encord and would appreciate
another chance to prove ourselves.

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

subject: Re: DL-RFP-2026-001 - Trial Account Access
text:
Hi William,

Understood regarding the trial process, we'll align internally on next
steps and follow up.

In the meantime, our engineering team reviewed your RFP response and needs
clarification on the deployment model. Your proposal describes a
cloud-hosted deployment managed by Encord, but the stated prerequisites - a
Pinterest-controlled AWS account with IAM permissions to provision
Kubernetes, databases, storage, load balancers, and certificates, plus
operator tooling (Terraform, Helm, kubectl, awscli) on our side - describe
infrastructure we would own and operate. For reference, past providers have
only required S3 bucket access from us.

Could you clarify:

   1. Do these prerequisites apply to the managed offering in your
   proposal, or to a different deployment option?
   2. If they apply, what runs in Pinterest's AWS account versus Encord's,
   and who is operationally responsible for each?

A written answer here would be helpful, as it directly affects how we
assess security, cost, and operational burden in the evaluation.

Thanks,

*Robel Djerrahian* (he/him) 📌

*Strategic Sourcing Specialist II*

rartin@pinterest.com
